title: Preregistered evaluation of generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipelines for NetOps configuration safety in an emulated testbed
research_question: Does an integrated generate→verify→repair (GVR) pipeline combining a hosted LLM generator, a deterministic network verifier, and an automated repair loop reduce unsafe or incorrect network changes (verifier-detectable property violations and simulated rollout failures) versus LLM-only generation on paired intent-to-change tasks in an emulated production-like NetOps testbed?
confirmatory_hypotheses: H1: The GVR pipeline yields a higher final simulated-correctness rate (fraction of tasks whose final enacted configuration satisfies all preregistered verifier properties) than LLM-only generation on the same intent items (paired design).
H2: For verifier-detectable violations that occur in the initial generation, the automated GVR repair loop resolves >90% within one repair iteration for the preregistered task suite.
exploratory_questions: E1: How do GVR gains vary by topology scale (small / medium / large emulations)?
E2: What are root-cause attributions for residual unsafe outcomes (verifier-coverage gap, ambiguous intent, generator error)?
E3: How much of observed variance is attributable to hosted-model nondeterminism?
benchmark_scope: Emulated containerized router/switch testbed with programmable ACLs, BGP/OSPF, VLANs and deterministic packet-level reachability checks
Intent-to-configuration change tasks sampled from publicly documented NetOps task templates and synthetic variants (no private production data)
model_scope: Primary: single hosted LLM (stable model identifier recorded in Disclosure) used for full paired experiment
Robustness check: one additional hosted smaller model (same provider family or another hosted API) applied to a preregistered random subset (30 tasks) for a small multi-model check
transformation_scope: Prompt-to-configuration parsing and canonicalization (token-level normalization, whitespace/indent normalization, CLI token mapping)
Automated repair-prompt templates that re-invoke the same hosted LLM with verifier feedback (up to two repair iterations)
primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in final simulated-correctness probability (GVR minus LLM-only) across the preregistered N=120 intent tasks.
secondary_estimands: Proportion of initial verifier-detectable violations resolved within one repair iteration (GVR pipeline).
Distribution (median, IQR) of repair iterations per task in GVR.
sampling_plan: Confirmatory task set N=120 unique intent-to-change items sampled deterministically from the preregistered task generator and stratified equally across three topology scales: small=40, medium=40, large=40 (40*3=120). Each intent is executed once under each pipeline (paired design): for pipeline A (LLM-only) and pipeline B (GVR). A separate verifier-coverage testset (oracle/unit tasks) of 30 items enumerates property-classes the verifier fully supports; these unit tasks exercise reachability, ACL policy conformance, and BGP-origin constraints (no model calls required). Total confirmatory executions: 120 tasks × 2 pipelines = 240 pipeline executions. Planned task-to-model invocation mapping and counts are in budget scenarios.
analysis_plan: Primary analysis: paired binary outcome (final simulated-correctness) per task; use McNemar's exact test for paired differences and report absolute risk reduction with two-sided 95% Wilson CIs. Secondary analyses: compute proportion of repairs resolved within one iteration with 95% CIs; stratified analyses by topology scale using conditional logistic regression or stratified McNemar where appropriate. Report exact p-values. Exploratory subgroup tests controlled via Benjamini–Hochberg (q=0.05). Provide descriptive latency and model-call counts (median, IQR). Report both per-protocol (completed pairs) and sensitivity analyses that impute technical-failure outcomes conservatively (worst-case imputation and best-case). All analysis code and raw outputs will be archived.
multiplicity_plan: Primary outcome (H1) is pre-specified and confirmatory. Secondary estimands are confirmatory for H2 only. All other subgroup and exploratory tests are labeled exploratory; multiplicity control for exploratory lists uses Benjamini–Hochberg at q=0.05. Exact confirmatory tests: one primary test (H1) and one confirmatory secondary test (H2).
missingness_plan: Technical/API failures: automatic retry policy of up to 2 retries per failed model invocation with exponential backoff (0s, 5s, 15s). If after retries the call fails, mark the pipeline execution as 'technical_failure' and exclude that pipeline run from the paired analysis for the primary confirmatory McNemar test. Automatically log and publish counts of technical failures. Sensitivity analyses: (a) complete-case (per-protocol) analysis using paired tasks with both pipelines completed; (b) worst-case imputation (treat missing GVR as failure and missing LLM-only as success) and opposite best-case to bracket effects. No manual adjudication will be used; all inclusion/exclusion decisions are deterministic and recorded.

risk_factors: Hosted-model non-determinism (API-side sampling variance or model-version changes)
Task leakage due to model pretraining (unknown overlap between synthetic prompts and model training data)
Unmodeled verifier limitations (property classes not supported)
detection_procedures: Record model API response hashes and entire response text for each call; compute per-item output-identity checksums to detect identical repeated outputs.
Log model API version headers and timestamps to detect provider-side version changes.
Run verifier-coverage unit tests and produce a per-property support matrix (automated PASS/FAIL per unit test).
Monitor API error codes and rate-limit responses and flag any runs exceeding preregistered retry counts.
item_flagging_rules: Flag item as 'nondeterminism-suspect' if repeated identical prompts produce differing verifier outcomes across retries.
Flag item as 'provider-version-change' if model-version header differs from preregistered identifier during execution.
Flag item as 'verifier-unsupported-property' if unit tests indicate the property-class is unsupported; such items are excluded from attribution claims (but remain in observed outcomes).
contamination_plan.analysis_treatment: Primary analysis excludes items flagged as technical failures per missingness_plan. Items flagged for provider-version-change will be reported and included only in sensitivity analyses; primary confirmatory test will use the preregistered run window (single contiguous execution window). For items with verifier-unsupported properties, report outcomes but analyze them separately and do not attribute residual failures to GVR efficacy. Nondeterminism-suspect items will be examined automatically (reporting counts) and included in sensitivity analyses.
residual_uncertainty: Unknown overlap between task prompts and model training data may bias model performance estimates.
Residual untested verifier property-classes may explain some GVR residual failures.

budget_scenarios.description: Minimal planned model-call budget sufficient to execute the preregistered paired experiment with a small robustness subset and reserve for retries.
transformations: repair_prompt_iteration (1 additional call per repair iteration, up to 2)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Under capability manifest: hosted-model API available, CPU and docker for verifier/emulator. Planned worst-case call budget fits well below capability limit (10,000). Scenario plans for retries and robustness subset. Model-call budget derivation: confirmatory executions = 120 tasks × 2 pipelines = 240 pipeline executions. Call accounting (worst-case): LLM-only pipeline: 120 generation calls. GVR pipeline: 120 initial generation calls + up to 2 repair calls/task = up to 360 calls. Robustness subset: 30 extra calls to secondary hosted model. Total worst-case = 120 + 360 + 30 = 510. Add 190-call buffer for prompt-tuning, debug runs, and audit logs = 700 planned calls.

budget_scenarios.description: Recommended scenario with conservative buffer for nondeterminism auditing and extended robustness checks (preferred).
transformations: robustness_subset_multi-call diagnostics (up to 3 calls per selected item for variance estimation)
budget_scenarios.feasibility_rationale: Same derivation as minimal scenario plus expanded diagnostics: planned base worst-case calls = 510 (see minimal). Additional diagnostics: re-sampling of 30 robustness-subset items up to 3 times each (30×2 extra calls = 60) to measure within-item nondeterminism, plus 200-call buffer for prompt-probing and logging = 510+60+200=770; rounded to 1200 to preserve headroom for provider-side transient retries within the 2-retry policy. This remains well within capability manifest max model-calls=10000.

power_plan.primary_estimand: Paired absolute difference in final simulated-correctness probability (GVR minus LLM-only) across N=120 tasks.
power_plan.target_effect: Detect an absolute improvement of 0.15 (15 percentage points) in final correctness with two-sided alpha=0.05 and power ≈0.8 under conservative discordant-pair assumptions.
power_plan.clustering_unit: Individual intent task (paired across two pipelines).
power_plan.calculation_method: Approximate paired/sample-size reasoning for McNemar's test: under assumed discordant proportions p01=0.20 (fails under LLM-only, corrected under GVR) and p10=0.05 (opposite), sample N≈100 achieves ~80% power; preregistered N=120 provides margin for technical failures and subgroup analyses.
assumptions: Paired design with independent task-level outcomes
Primary discordant-pair assumption: p01−p10≈0.15 for target effect
Per-task outcomes deterministically recorded; technical failures excluded from primary paired test but reported
power_plan.minimum_detectable_effect_notes: With N=120, the minimum detectable paired absolute difference is approximately 0.12–0.18 depending on observed within-pair discordance; sensitivity analyses will report exact MDE given observed discordant counts.
sensitivity_analyses: Recompute power/post-hoc MDE given observed discordant counts and produce 95% CIs for the absolute risk reduction.
Report per-scale (small/medium/large) MDEs; treat these as exploratory if underpowered.

transformation_families: CLI parsing and canonicalization (indentation/whitespace normalization, token canonical mapping)
Configuration AST mapping for verifier input (structured representation)
semantic_equivalence_checks: Round-trip: generated CLI → AST → rendered CLI → AST equality checks (automated) for syntactic equivalence
Verifier acceptance: a transformation is considered semantically acceptable if the verifier accepts the rendered AST for the preregistered property-class
Automated differential-checks across canonicalizers to detect loss of semantics (e.g., ACL ordering changes that alter semantics)
automatic_rejection_rules: Reject generated configuration if parsing fails or mandatory fields (interface identifiers, ACL IDs, route-targets) are missing; the pipeline will automatically return a structured 'parse_fail' outcome and, in GVR, trigger repair iteration.
Reject and flag any configuration that changes property-classes outside the intent specification (e.g., introduces new ACLs not requested) via deterministic token checks.
transformation_validation.audit_sample_policy: 100% automatic checks for syntactic parseability; additional automated deep-audit on a 10% random sample of successfully parsed transformations using packet-level reachability simulation and cross-verifier consistency checks.
transformation_validation.mapping_validation: Maintain canonical token mapping tables (interface aliases, vendor-agnostic names) and validate mapping deterministically against the verifier AST schema; failures are automatically flagged and logged.
residual_risks: Vendor-specific CLI semantics (ordering-dependent commands, implicit defaults) may not be fully captured by canonicalization and can produce semantic drift.
Certain high-level operational intents (e.g., intended partial-rollout semantics) are not directly encoded as verifier properties and remain a source of residual misinterpretation.

remaining_noncritical_uncertainties: Emulator fidelity: vendor-specific CLI semantics and rollback behaviors are only approximated; external validity to specific vendor environments is limited and documented.

Residual verifier-coverage limits: despite unit tests, some operational invariants (timing-dependent behaviors, vendor implicit defaults) may remain untestable by the verifier and will be reported separately.
Single-hosted-model generalizability: a small multi-model robustness subset mitigates but does not eliminate generalizability limits across the broader model population.
Possible training-data overlap between synthetic prompts and model training corpora (unknown) may bias generator performance estimates.
